geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the existing dominant mass in a courtyard macro so the public void becomes explicit and program-supporting.
Make the court large enough to function as a real open-space figure.
Open the court toward the access edge to improve frontage legibility and public entry.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the upper setback logic into a more legible public court condition while preserving the dominant bent-bar ancestry and improving neighborhood public-space support.
Enlarge the carved open space so it reads as usable public void rather than shallow terracing.
Align the court opening with the verified access side to strengthen the street threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently across views as one continuous bent-and-stepped mass, so gesture and hierarchy are solid. It does respond to the parcel in a general way, but the open-space figure is still mostly implied by stepping rather than a clearly public court or undercut. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly: the mass does not yet make a decisive street threshold or entry seam toward access. Program-wise, this can plausibly support neighborhood living because it is compact, low-rise, and not a misfit tower/hall typology, but the section is still too close to an abstract terraced object rather than a street-active mixed-use building with a clear ground condition. References consistently support courtyard/terrace/bridge languages, which this candidate partly echoes, though not yet with enough void-public legibility.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a large central void and bridge-like upper connection; good precedent for a compact neighborhood program with a legible public opening.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much larger and more campus-scaled than the candidate; do not copy its multi-building scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced campus-like arrangement around a central courtyard; useful for understanding how stepped masses can organize public open space.
Elongated low-rise mass with a central atrium/courtyard and folded roof logic; supports a horizontally spread neighborhood program.
Terraced ribbon composition with connected wings and a clear public interior sequence; strong transferable logic for active circulation and stepped section.
Interlocking wings with a courtyard void and setback upper masses; useful as a massing principle for preserving hierarchy while carving public space.
